To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bond strength is higher for vibrated concrete than for self-compacting concrete, and the bond strength depends on the plastic stress level in the concrete.
the bond between self-compacting concrete and steel in columns with stirrups and without stirrups is better than between vibrated concrete.
the bond between concrete with different compaction method and steel in composite column is influenced by the concrete plastic stress level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the bond between steel sections and concrete.
the bond between concrete (vibrated and self-compacting) and steel in composite column.
the assessment of the bond between the concrete and the steel in composite columns and with the development of a numerical model of such columns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bond in the case of vibrated concrete is better than that for the self-compacting concrete, but in both cases it is possible to design the composite column according to the EC 4.
the bond between concrete (compacted by vibration) and steel in composite beams is better than in the case of self-compacted concrete.
in case of vibrated concrete a better bond is obtained.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bond between steel reinforcement and concrete in composite column is better for vibrated concrete than for self-compacting concrete and it is possible to model this bond using the FE method.
the compaction method is important and the bond between concrete core and steel should be considered in the design of composite columns.
the bond between concrete in composite columns is influenced by both the type of concrete and the compaction method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the compaction method is of importance for bond strength.
the bond between steel reinforcement and concrete is influenced by the method of concrete compaction.
the bond strength between steel and concrete is a function of the concrete compressive strength.
